headline: An Indian AI computing company backed by the founders of Greenko has reportedly ordered 20,000 of Nvidia's newest Rubin chips in a deal worth about $4 billion.
score_reason: Based on two unnamed sources with no confirmation yet; kept at the pool level.
importance_line: It signals how fast India is building AI computing capacity, which affects Indian AI developers and power planners, but the order is unconfirmed and the company has yet to announce it.
summary: Mint reports, citing two people aware of the matter, that AM Intelligence, backed by the founders of Greenko, has placed a binding order for 20,000 Nvidia Rubin graphics processors (GPUs, the chips that train and run AI models) worth around $4 billion, to supply 70 megawatts of computing power across India and Malaysia. The companies have not confirmed the order, and Mint says Nvidia and the Greenko-linked firms did not respond to its queries.
notes: URL is the TradingView copy of Mint's text; original Mint link not found.
